articles.title: White Sox to Use Two Regular Season Starters in Game 2 Against Guardians
articles.summary: The Chicago White Sox will start Anthony Kay on Monday as they look to steal a second game in Cleveland.
articles.body:
As terrific as Grant Taylor was in closing out Game 1 of the ALDS , he threw enough pitches that it's extremely unlikely that we'll see him in Game 2, even with a scheduled day off. Consequently, the White Sox have opted to return to a pitching strategy that has worked several times for them this season.

Will Venable has shown time and again that he is not afraid to go outside the traditional pitching structure. And hey, if it's gotten the Sox this far, why should he even think about stopping it now? The plan for Game 2 indicates that he won't.

Will Venable has announced that Anthony Kay will open for Sean Burke in Game 2 . It's a clearer pitching plan than what was announced before Game 1, which was that Hagen Smith would start with no indication of how long he would go. It turned out he got the first eight outs before losing control and being removed.

During the regular season, Kay started four games against the Cleveland Guardians and went 1-0 with a 1.35 ERA and a 0.95 WHIP. In Game 1, he entered with two outs and one runner on in the fourth inning, then loaded the bases before escaping the jam. He pitched a perfect fifth before Taylor brought the Sox home.

Kay's earlier dominance of the Guardians has continued so far, and the Sox hope that will be the case Burke, too. He was 2-0 with a 1.34 ERA, 21 strikeouts, three walks, and a 1.15 WHIP. Sean Newcomb opened for him in his last appearance in Cleveland on Sept. 14, and he got the win by giving up no earned runs on four hits over five-plus innings.

Of all the Sox pitchers who started against the Guardians this season, Kay and Burke were the only two who had sub-2.00 ERAs in these games. It makes sense for Venable to pair these two up to try to steal both games on the road. If it works, he can be a little more flexible when preparing his pitching plan for Game 3.

The obvious goal here is to win Game 2 so that there can be two chances to clinch the series at home. But even if it doesn't work, the Guardians still need to win one game in Chicago to advance to the ALCS. The Sox are in a great spot, and superb pitching in Game 2 would make it an excellent spot.

articles.title: Marvel Unlimited Shutting Down, Will Be Replaced by 'Marvel Comics Powered by Webtoon'
articles.summary: Marvel Unlimited, the company's subscription app for comics, will be shuttering on December 17, 2026, after about 19 years of service.
articles.body:
Marvel Unlimited , the company's subscription app for comics, will be shuttering on December 17, 2026, after about 19 years of service.

Marvel annonced that new subscriptions for Unlimited would be ending today, and will be replaced by a new comics app, Marvel Comics Powered by Webtoon, on November 16, 2026. The service won't be taken fully offline until December, and existing subscribers will have free access to the app until it shuts down. If you were charged recently, that'll be the last time you're charged until the app shuts down. Marvel will also be sending users a prorated refund on November 16 for any remaining value on their subscription.

There is some overlap between Marvel Unlimited shuttering and the new app going online, and in that window, you'll be able to migrate your library over to the new Marvel Comics app, along with your reading progress. The mechanics of that transfer aren't clear, but in the email Marvel sent to subscribers it says, "Stay tuned to your inbox and in-app messages for more details on how to migrate your library by signing up with Webtoon."

For its part, the new Webtoon app seems like it may be an improvement over Marvel Unlimited, as long as you're willing to pay for a higher tier. The Ultimate tier will get access to new issues as soon as 30 days after they go to print, which is a huge improvement over the 3 months that the standard tier will have and that Unlimited had during its entire existence.

Marvel's Incursions One-Shots Preview Gallery

Ahead of the Webtoon app's release, it does look like the UI is a bit more modern, but that's just based on some initial screenshots. I've always had a problem with the way comics worked both on a smartphone and on a web browser in Unlimited, so if the Webtoon app is able to solve that, the migration will be worth it for me.

Luckily, the prices are mostly staying the same, too. I was paying $9.99 a month for Marvel Unlimited, and that's the same price that Webtoon's Base subscription will cost. That'll get you access to the full library and new issues 90 days after print. Or, you can get the Ultimate tier for $12.49 a month, which has the same library as the Base tier, just with new issues being added 30 days after print.

You can preorder the a year of the Ultimate tier for $59.99 , which works out to $4.99 for the first year. That's much cheaper than the Base tier, but it will renew at $99.99 after the first year.

articles.title: Physint Update: Hideo Kojima Shares New Info on His Upcoming Metal Gear Spiritual Successor
articles.summary: Renowned game director Hideo Kojima revived his Koji10 podcast after a year and shared casting, story, and development updates on Physint, his upcoming next-generation action-espionage game and spiritual successor to Metal Gear Solid.
articles.body:
Renowned game director Hideo Kojima revived his Koji10 podcast after a year and shared casting, story, and development updates on Physint, his upcoming next-generation action-espionage game and spiritual successor to Metal Gear Solid.

Thanks to a summary of the 79-minute English-subtitled podcast on YouTube by X user Genki_JPN, we now know a bit more about the status of Physint, which made huge headlines recently after Kojima revealed that Sony was set to cancel the project as its publisher, leading to Microsoft picking it up . Kojima describes Physint as a project to commemorate his 40th anniversary as a game developer. He said he wants it to evoke the roots of the Metal Gear Solid games, but be a new interactive experience with a different kind of spy action. He aims to fill it with lots of new ideas.

Story and cast-wise, Kojima says he has the plot already and that he pitched all of the actors appearing in it himself – 70% of whom are apparently Kojima fans. Many of the character names have been decided Filming will start next year, with Bill Skarsgard , Charlie Fraser and Minami Hamabe already scanned.

Finally, the 63-year-old Kojima said that he makes every one of his games as if it could be his last.

The other game Kojima is developing for Microsoft, the PT spiritual successor OD, is expected to be released before Physint, which Kojima himself said was 5-6 years away last year.

articles.title: Final Fantasy 7 Revelation Hot Springs Scenes Reveal New Bathing Suit Skins for the Party
articles.summary: New Final Fantasy 7 Revelation footage has revealed a hot springs feature that boosts the party's health and gives them a set of new bathing suit skins.
articles.body:
New Final Fantasy 7 Revelation footage has revealed a hot springs feature that boosts the party's health and gives them a set of new bathing suit skins.

Half the fun of Square Enix's remake trilogy is allowing Cloud, Barret, Tifa, and the rest of the party to have some fun on their way to stop Sephiroth once and for all. In Rebirth , that meant spending a day at the beach , and in Final Fantasy 7 Revelation, players will be able to kick their feet up, mingle, and, for some reason, balance rubber Chocobos at a collection of new hot springs.

The publisher unveiled the new gameplay feature as part of SDCC Málaga and later shared gameplay footage on social media. When the group stops at a hot spring, they'll benefit from a permanent increase to their max HP. The health bonus and moments shared between each character seem to be the real draw. The thing that might appeal to some players more than others, though, is the promise that the bathing suit outfits featured during these segments can be unlocked as skins, too.

Across all of the clips shown online today, we can see skins for Cloud, Barret, and Cid. Red XIII can relax in the hot springs, too, but considering he's not usually wearing clothes to begin with, it doesn't look like any skin he may get will change his appearance too much. Then, there's newly playable party member Vincent Valentine, who prefers to bathe in the same slick get-up he fights monsters in because he's… just that cool, I guess.

"We’re sharing a preview of some of the hot spring events revealed during our stage presentation at SDCC Málaga," director Naoki Hamaguchi said in a follow-up post on X/Twitter. "Each hot spring offers a different glimpse into the characters’ everyday lives, and the outfits featured in these events can also be unlocked as skins. Explore the world, discover hot springs, and enjoy these special moments with your companions!"

Final Fantasy 7 Revelation is still months from delivering the concluding chapter of the remake trilogy, but that hasn't stopped Square Enix from unloading new details as often as it can manage. Hamaguchi has been especially keen to share, telling IGN last month that players will have an option to automatically level up their characters if they want to skip the grind. He's also said players could easily spend more than 100 hours playing through the story , even if the Platinum Trophy doesn't present much of a challenge on its own .

Final Fantasy 7 Revelation launches for PC, Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S April 8, 2027. While we wait to see how those hot springs heat things up for Cloud and company, you can see how Hamaguchi responded to players hoping for a full-disc release . articles.title: RuneScape Dev Pulls Trailer After 6-Fingered Knight Leads to Generative AI Allegations
articles.summary: RuneScape developer Jagex has pulled a new trailer after a six-fingered knight led to allegations of generative AI use from fans.
articles.body:
RuneScape developer Jagex has pulled a new trailer after a six-fingered knight led to allegations of generative AI usage from fans.

There were some ups and downs for RuneScape players over the weekend. What started with a string of big reveals from RuneFest 2026 ended with social media users voicing their concern that generative AI had been used to make the new trailer for RuneScape 3 's Dragon Slayer 2 quest.

The backlash was loud enough that Jagex stepped in not only to release an official response on the matter but also to pull the trailer entirely while it investigates "urgently." The statement, posted on Reddit by social media manager Alex Sween (via Kotaku ), acknowledged some of the more undeniable concerns related to the trailer – including the fact that one of its knights has six fingers.

"Hello, it’s me, again, talking about Gen AI, again," the statement began, referencing a separate, recent incident involving 100 Thieves and OSRS . The team also took a "hard line stance" against generative AI earlier this year. "We’re aware of the concerns raised about the Dragon Slayer 2 trailer and have taken it down, while we investigate urgently. This trailer was produced by a trusted external partner who had explicitly confirmed that GenAI would not be used. But, among other things, there’s a sixth finger and, well, that’s pretty hard to explain away. For that we apologise.

Although uploads of RuneScape's Dragon Slayer 2 trailer can no longer be found on official channels, it is still available via the full RuneFest 2026 livestream . There are also plenty of posts from fans discussing the matter still live across social media. They're not happy, but Jagex knows that.

The team took its statement and apology as an opportunity to, again, make its position clear: "We don't use GenAI to create our games, artwork, or creative assets and will not knowingly allow it to be used on our behalf." However, it's hard to deny that a second instance of artificial intelligence being used to generate content suggests a deeper problem for the MMO developer. Jagex explained that it plans to address its approach to working with partners going forward.

Then today, Jagex decided to use AI in a trailer for an upcoming quest, the knight in video has 6 fingers and boots in a another frame look like modern sneakers. — TheNoobishDad (@ABNreaper) October 4, 2026

Then today, Jagex decided to use AI in a trailer for an upcoming quest, the knight in video has 6 fingers and boots in a another frame look like modern sneakers.

"Immediately following RuneFest we’re overhauling our review processes," the statement continued, "and we’re going to work with and commission creators from the community to make sure that the story of Dragon Slayer 2 is told to the standard befitting of such an update."

The six-fingered knight really does feel like the smoking gun, but another bizarre piece of art from the trailer, which showed a fully-armored knight wearing what seemed to be a regular old pair of tennis shoes, had fans raising eyebrows, too. In follow-up replies, Sween acknowledged it's something Jagex "should have caught," adding, "We didn't do well enough and can't simply place the blame elsewhere."

As Jagex refines its processes to maintain its stance against generative AI, it's still working to deliver other new projects. RuneScape 4 is one of these new projects, with an animated adaptation also in the works with YouTuber MoistCr1tikal.

articles.title: Infinity Ward Details Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's Extraction Mode, DMZ
articles.summary: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's ambitious new extraction mode, DMZ, has gotten a massive deep dive from Infinity Ward.
articles.body:
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's ambitious new extraction mode, DMZ, has received a massive deep dive from Infinity Ward.

DMZ was initially introduced in 2022's Modern Warfare II, and now, with the rise in popularity of extraction shooters, it is coming back in a bigger way . The mode is expected to be a major part of Modern Warfare 4's offerings, with its own 70-level progression system, lucrative rewards, and world building/lore. Additionally, there will be a forward operating base for players to hang out in between matches. Here, players can practice at a firing range to test their loadouts, craft items based on loot they've found in the world, gain intel and track different missions, bosses, and unique challenges for their next deployment, and more.

Speaking in a new behind-the-scenes video, Infinity Ward co-studio head Jack O'Hara stated that fans made it clear that there weren't high enough stakes in the first iteration of DMZ, so they've worked to change that. For starters, your time in DMZ is defined by your operator. This is a character that you build and level up, but if they die, it will cost you to bring them back. There are also lootable items that can be permanently lost if the player dies or drops them. These items can be used at a 3D printer to craft things like armor plates, consumables, gear, and seemingly killstreaks or AI-controlled fire support, based on a menu seen in some gameplay.

The team behind DMZ also described it as an "action extraction shooter." Infinity Ward wants players to feel like there is constant danger both through AI combatants, bosses, and other players, so you won't spend a ton of time wandering around opening boxes with minimal friction. Infinity Ward laid out a plethora of different enemy types in a blog post , noting that there will be drones, helicopter and vehicle patrols, tanks, and tougher enemies.

Different parts of the map will have different threat levels, and those levels can rise based on the player's actions. If you're running around causing a bunch of noise, it will create more attention and lead to enemies searching for you. However, if you play stealtihly with silenced weapons, melee takedowns, and exercise caution, you can avoid extreme conflict. Additionally, the more players explore, the more opportunities there will be to uncover loot and secrets in the game's world.

Infinity Ward has also promised extensive support for DMZ post-launch, including changes to the map, dynamic weather that can vary per season, and much more. It sounds like a big focus for the team and it should be a really cool change for Call of Duty. Hopefully it sticks and isn't dropped next year, but that will likely depend on if players show up to support it.

DMZ will be available at launch when Modern Warfare 4 releases on October 23. Unlike MWII's version, it will not be free-to-play.

articles.title: Hideo Kojima Says You'll See Him Cameo in a 'Big' Live-Action Movie — But Which One Is It?
articles.summary: Hideo Kojima teased that he's got a cameo in a "big" live-action movie, but he's not saying which one we'll see him in quite yet.
articles.body:
Hideo Kojima teased that he's got a cameo in a "big" live-action movie, but he's not saying which one we'll see him in quite yet.

The Metal Gear Solid and Death Stranding creator enticed film fans to theorize about his movie career during a surprise installment in the Koji10 podcast . In between talking about Physint and what's next for his Kojima Productions, the famed game developer revealed that he would appear in movie theaters as part of a big new live-action movie cameo.

"I already shot a few other things," Kojima said, as translated through YouTube's English captions (via @Genki_JPN ). "Directors and others have asked me to."

The topic came up when reminiscing about his time doing voice acting work as a mole in Zootopia 2 . While the Japanese version of the Pixar film had him provide his talents behind the scenes, he suggested this mysterious new project will allow him to be in front of the camera in some capacity.

So as not to spoil the surprise, he said he "can't say" what it is yet, but it is a "big movie." It is indeed live-action, too, but his involvement is so secretive for now that he even refused to tell his hosts where he shot his part.

Kojima is best known for his work as a game developer, but he's also a well-read cinephile, too. Fans routinely turn up for his reviews of movies like Superman , Backrooms , Spider-Man: Brand New Day , and more. Even his social media biography jokes that "70% of my body is made of movies," so it's no surprise to see him continue to be as involved in film as he can manage.

Many have also already started speculating when exactly we'll see Kojima show up, too, even if no one has any truly solid leads to go on yet. Some have guessed we'll see him in Denis Villeneuve's Dune: Part 3 this December, while others suggested he'll show up in The Legend of Zelda movie , or even next month's Godzilla Minus Zero . Other guesses come from those who are just happy to see their favorite game creator show up in live-action at all.

"Hideo Kojima will return in Avengers: Doomsday," one fan said .

Kojima also said his future in entertainment will see him in not one but two "major anime" titles. These are "really big" but still a mystery for audiences for now, with the developer only saying that he has speaking lines coming up. He also said that an upcoming game cameo – a concept that is far from new for him – is also a secret, though fans have already found evidence that he's been scanned for Naughty Dog's Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet .

In terms of Kojima's main occupation, he's still very much at work on his new espionage action game, Physint. He offered an update on the Bill Skarsgård-starring title's progress during today's podcast, too, teasing that many of the characters' names have already been decided, and their actors scanned. He's also still heads-down working on his horror game, OD .

articles.title: Disastrous defense sinks Yankees in ALDS Game 2 loss to Rays
articles.summary: For the second time in three years, the Yankees had a disastrous defensive game in the postseason and it cost them again, this time in a 5-2 loss to the Rays...
articles.body:
For the second time in three years, the Yankees had a disastrous defensive game in the postseason and it cost them again, this time in a 5-2 loss to the Rays Monday night in Game 2 of the AL Division Series.

The Yanks made four errors in the loss, leading to three unearned runs, and they now teeter on the brink of elimination, down two games to none in the best-of-five series. Game 3 is set for Wednesday night at Yankee Stadium.

Two years ago, the Yankee defense collapsed in Game 5 of the World Series against the Dodgers and they were eliminated. But even that game only featured three Yankee errors – in the box score, anyway.

Monday's debacle was only the fifth time the Yankees have made four errors in a single postseason game. The last time was in the 2019 ALCS against the Astros.

The Yankees have scored only twice so far in the series, on two solo home runs by Ben Rice Monday night. No Aaron Judge , who is out with a calf injury, certainly doesn't help.

Yankee starter Cam Schlittler was not nearly as brilliant as he's been in his previous postseason outings. He lasted just 4.1 innings and allowed seven hits and four runs (only two earned). He struck out just two and didn't have a strikeout until the fourth inning and got only seven swings-and-misses. He also walked one. His career postseason ERA rose from 0.87 to 1.44.

The Yankees defensive implosion started in the very first inning and set a dubious club record for errors in a single postseason frame – three. The Yankees had never had three errors in one October inning and this is the 61st postseason appearance in the Yankees' existence. The Yanks last committed three errors in an inning in any game on Aug. 21, 2025 against the Red Sox. The last time it happened in any postseason game was Game 5 of the 2015 ALDS when the Rangers did it in a loss to the Blue Jays.

Ryan McMahon , who has a fine defensive reputation, though he has not had his best season with the glove, made the first miscue when the leadoff hitter, Yandy Díaz , hit a topspin bouncer to him that McMahon muffed. Jonathan Aranda followed with a single and then Junior Caminero hit what could've been a double-play grounder to short. George Lombard Jr. made a not-that-graceful flip to the bag and Jazz Chisholm Jr. grabbed it and threw wildly to first. Díaz scored and Caminero went to second.

Then it seemed like Schlittler had Hicks struck out, but, upon replay review, Austin Wells was called for catcher's interference – his mitt was clearly in the path of Hicks' bat. That was the third error of the inning. They nearly had a fourth – Chisholm fielded Simpson's grounder but threw high to second base, pulling Lombard off the bag. But Lombard got back in time for a force out. Schlittler got a grounder from Victor Mesa to mercifully end the inning. The Yankees only allowed one run, but all the gaffes forced Schlittler to endure some tense moments and extra pitches.

The Rays scored four runs in the fifth inning and knocked out Schlittler. They got some weak contact and used their speed to exploit it. Poor Yankee defense helped, too. Aranda started the inning with a single and Caminero followed with a ringing double. With the infield mostly in – Chisholm was further back than the rest of the infielders – Liam Hicks hit a grounder that was slow enough to allow Aranda to score.

Chandler Simpson later hit a soft grounder to short that Lombard couldn't backhand and another run scored. The scoring on that play was changed several times, but it was ultimately scored a fielder's choice. But Lombard then made a throwing error to further prolong the inning and Richie Palacios added a single after an eight-pitch bout with reliever Brent Headrick that scored two more runs.

The Yanks went nine up, nine down the first time through their batting order as Rays starter Freddy Peralta looked sharp. But Rice tied the score at 1 with a 372-foot drive over the right-field fence. Rice connected on the fourth of four consecutive changeups from Peralta. Rice also homered in the eighth inning, giving him four home runs in four games this postseason.

In the fifth, the Yanks had a big chance with two outs, but could not cash in. Wells lashed a double into the right-field corner that looked a lot like the ball he hit in Game 1 and got thrown out trying to stretch into a triple. He wisely stopped at second this time. McMahon then worked a walk in a tough, seven-pitch at-bat. He was the last batter that Peralta faced. He came out with Rice coming up to the plate.

Rice worked another walk against southpaw Cam Booser , which brought up Cody Bellinger , who was 11th in MLB this season with a .340 average with runners in scoring position. Bellinger hit a deep fly ball to the warning track in center that held some hope, but it was caught.

Peralta, the former Met who got his pitching together in Tampa Bay, lasted 4.2 innings and allowed one run and three hits. He struck out three and walked one. The outing lowered his career postseason ERA from 4.32 to 4.03.

The Yankees return home to New York with Game 3 of the ALDS against the Rays on Wednesday at 8:00 p.m.

articles.title: Yankees' defensive miscues wipe away golden opportunity to even ALDS
articles.summary: The Yankees played such historically porous defense Monday that they rendered their most dominant playoff ace in a generation completely irrelevant with seve...
articles.body:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. -- For a moment, before all the accountability cliches started flowing for the cameras in the Yankees ' clubhouse, Cam Schlittler was blunt.

"I'll be the first one to say that I didn't do my job," the 25-year-old ace said. "But it didn't seem like we really showed up today."

Given the chance to double down later, Schlittler wouldn't do it.

"The guys work their asses off," he explained.

He wasn't good enough, either, of course.

But in reality, the Yankees played such historically porous defense Monday that they rendered their most dominant playoff ace in a generation completely irrelevant with several defensive misplays including four errors.

At one point, they set the record for most errors in a single Yankee playoff game with five -- only to have the fifth error overturned by the official scorer.

"Obviously, a really rough night to say the least for us," manager Aaron Boone said. "We've got to get over it. We've responded all year to difficult times, and we've got to do that again. We've got to get ourselves up off the mat."

Boone said he would address the players when they were settled on the plane back to New York early Tuesday morning. At times in describing what happened, he seemed lost for words, though he always found his way back to "we got to get over it, though. As simple as that."

What will be difficult to get over is that the Yankees' inability cost them the game they seemed most certain to win, one in which Schlittler started and his fellow playoff savant, Ben Rice , homered twice.

Playoff games include plenty of error-filled innings and misplays that end up ending seasons. But what the Yankees did Monday was not an example of natural ebb and flow.

Game 2 was a meltdown, the kind that can only be explained by something other than pure physical error -- something like when Aaron Judge dropped a fly ball in Game 5 of the 2024 World Series, for example. Twice can be coincidence, but it sure feels like a trend.

"The guys and I, we work hard. We go out there every day. We take our ground balls and we take them very seriously," Jazz Chisholm Jr. said. "… Especially certain guys that are defensive specialists, some of the best defenders I've ever played with are playing. So for me, it hurts us a little more than you'd think."

Monday's lineup was not the Yankees' best defensive alignment, but it hardly lined up as their worst either.

In fact, even after nearly being no-hit two nights ago, Boone decided to start Ryan McMahon in a platoon matchup against Freddy Peralta rather than start versatile Jose Caballero at third base or test novice Anthony Volpe there on unfamiliar turf. McMahon is an elite defender, which is why he starts there more often than not.

But when Yandy Diaz led off the game with a chopper his way, McMahon simply missed the easy hop, then looked as surprised as everyone else to discover he somehow had not caught it. More topspin than he thought, he said later.

Suddenly, Schlittler was in the stretch. Inevitably, he was not in peak rhythm. He was not the only one.

After a Jonathan Aranda single, Junior Caminero hit a groundball that George Lombard Jr. chased down up the middle. He flipped the ball to Chisholm, who caught it falling over second base and decided to throw to first base in the process. It bounced away.

Two batters later, Chisholm fielded a routine groundball that could have been a double play. He threw it high to Lombard cringing when he let go as if he wished he could pull it right back. The throw cost them a double play.

In between those two Chisholm plays, Austin Wells was called for catcher's interference on a pitch that would have been strike three. That the Rays scored just one run during what ended as a three-error first inning was a relative miracle, one due in part to Schlittler's composure.

Schlittler has been historically unflappable in big games during his first two postseasons. He is as calm as they come, and more confident than most.

Asked before the game if he had ever seen Schlittler doubt himself, for example, center fielder Trent Grisham did not hesitate.

But the Schlittler who found himself in the middle of a teamwide defensive meltdown looked as uncomfortable as he ever has in a game this important.

His velocity was not quite where it was in his Wild Card start. He searched for his fastball command, missing so badly up and inside to Diaz at one point in the second that he walked up to Diaz to talk about it afterward.

Everyone seemed to decide it had been completely accidental. After all, Schlittler had been missing wide with his fastball, as well.

Even so, he survived the second inning, then the third, then the fourth. A Rice homer meant the game was tied when he took the mound to start the fifth inning. Then the Yankees knocked their ace out of the game.

First, Spencer Jones got a late jump on a line drive to right. Caminero doubled. A soft ground ball to Chisholm (no one's fault) scored a run. A chopper to Lombard -- originally ruled an error, eventually ruled a fielder's choice -- scored another. Both plays would have required some heroics.

Too often, the Yankees could not do the basics.

"[Cam's] not wrong. Obviously, wasn't ideal from the start. We didn't make some plays we usually make, kind of happened throughout the game," Lombard said. "Just made it harder for ourselves."

Lombard threw a ball wide of first later that inning, so two runs scored on Richie Palacios ' single up the middle.

When it was all said and done, the Yankees had broken an ignominious team record and spurred Boone to try Brent Headrick to stop their bleeding. Schlittler finished after allowing four runs (two earned) on six hits in 4.1 innings.

The Rays applied their trademark pressure. The Yankees could not withstand it.

"I think [Cam's] just throwing a lot more pitches than he should have been throwing. I think it's maybe a different story there if we take care of the ball and he's at 30 pitches or 25, 30 pitches instead after the first two and gets in a rhythm and he's in a groove," Boone said. "Kind of found himself in trouble a lot tonight, not by his own doing."

Schlittler would be available to pitch Game 5 on Saturday if the Yankees can force it, but they will need to win two games to do that. Unfortunately for the Yankees, Monday's game -- like any game started by Schlittler, even when he is not at his best -- was supposed to be one of the games they could pencil in as a win.

Though Schlittler did not say so, it was his defense that beat him Monday.

"I'm not disappointed in our defense. I'm not disappointed in our offense," Schlittler said. "Really just disappointed in myself. That's baseball and those things are going to happen. I've got to be able to work through those. I wasn't able to do that today."

articles.title: Dominant Rays, wacky White Sox and Yanks flailing at the brink: ALDS takeaways
articles.summary: The Tampa Bay Rays and Chicago White Sox are both one win away from advancing to the AL Championship Series.
articles.body:
This year's American League Division Series have been significantly entertaining. And more than a little jarring.

The Tampa Bay Rays and Chicago White Sox are a combined 4-0, both one win away from advancing to the AL Championship Series, and both answering questions about their viability in a most voracious fashion.

And they're doing it their way, the White Sox with an unprecedented pitching plan and the Rays suffocating the New York Yankees in every facet of the game.

As the teams charter their way to New York and Chicago, here's five takeaways from a day that saw the Cleveland Guardians and New York Yankees pushed to the brink:

Best action from 2026 MLB playoffs' ALDS and NLDS

It's a tradition every autumn, trying to discern which teams' regular-season success will translate best to playoff baseball. The Rays have made two World Series runs in 18 years, the watchword in that time being their consistency.

This year, they rolled up 98 wins and the AL East title, yet every team must answer the same question once October arrives: Are they really that good?

Through two games, the answer seems to be, even better.

Tampa Bay's combo of speed and contact, and more than a little power, made them a tough out all season. And in two games against the Yankees, it's clear both of their offensive personalities are showing up.

Game 1 : Jonathan Aranda's solo homer provides the game's lone run.

Game 2 : The Yankees commit three first-inning errors and four overall , the last coming in a four-run fifth inning that turned a tie game into a solid Rays advantage and an eventual 5-2 victory.

You could say this was a Yankees problem, that they need to clean a lot of things up . And they do.

Yet the mere presence of Chandler Simpson, who plays faster than any human in the big leagues, was palpable in that fifth, when he hit a gentle two-hopper to Yankees shortstop George Lombard Jr., who had a generally impossible task: Throw out Junior Caminero running from third on a contact play or try to get Simpson streaking to first.

The answer: Neither. Lombard biffed the play, most likely properly ruled a fielder's choice, and Simpson was already clapping his hands five feet before he crossed first base.

"Constant pressure, constant long at-bats, getting pitches to hit. It's our MO all season long," manager Kevin Cash said in his postgame news conference. "We're a contact-oriented team with guys that can knock the ball out of the ballpark, as well."

And the Rays struck out just twice against Yankees ace Cam Schlittler, equaling a career low for the presumed Cy Young Award winner. Not an accident: No team struck out fewer times than Tampa Bay in the regular season.

The Yankees' bats are almost out of time

Talk about an unproductive business trip: The Yankees went 5-for-58 (.086) against the Rays in Games 1 and 2. Ben Rice hit a pair of homers in Game 2 .

The rest of their offense? There was none.

While there's really no point to the rest-vs.-rust argument for teams earning a first-round bye, the Rays certainly took advantage of their time off to develop a pitching plan against the Yankees. And it is being executed to perfection.

Never mind the 4⅔ serviceable innings Freddy Peralta worked. Lefty Ian Seymour – who toggled back and forth between bullpen and rotation this season – was practically untouchable in three relief innings, retiring nine of 10 batters, striking out four and yielding only a homer to the redoubtable Rice.

Funny thing about this wild-card era: Just finish a little above .500 and you can get in. Yet the gulfs between clubs can be massive. And while the Rays and Boston Red Sox shared a division, the similarities end there. New York scored 18 runs against Boston in the wild-card series, scarcely missing Aaron Judge.

It has scored two against the Rays. And the Yankees absolutely miss the big fella – and he ain't coming back for Game 3.

MLB teams ranked by their World Series championships

The White Sox have already made history: They're the first team in major league history to win their first four playoff games with their starting pitchers throwing four or fewer innings.

Yet in this era of openers and bulk guys and matchup-capturing, it hasn't felt gimmicky. Nor has it been panicky. Just feels like the White Sox manager and their personnel know exactly what they're doing.

Oh, Game 2 was plenty hairy: Lefty starter Anthony Kay got just one out, was removed for fellow lefty Sean Newcomb, who tossed a ball way wide of first and buried Chicago in a 2-0 hole as Cleveland's Progressive Field roared in the late-day sun.

Yet Venable's button-pushing and, essentially, his knowledge of his guys and the situation seems preternatural – and the dude's only managed four postseason games.

Think about it: In ALDS Game 1, right-hander Grant Taylor got a four-inning save.

Yeah, somehow Taylor for 42 pitches and 12 outs was the right call in a 3-0 Game 1 win .

And then, after just a day of rest, extending him for a four-out save – surviving a very hairy Jo Adell drive to the wall with a man on in the eighth – was also spot-on.

Taylor has worked in three of the White Sox's four games, absorbing eight innings. They used five pitchers each in Games 1 and 2, though Kay and Taylor were the only repeats.

That's not likely to stop so long as the White Sox are alive.

"I know we're pushing these guys, Grant especially," Venable said in his postgame press conference. "It is really a lot to ask, but he's in shape for this.

"He's ready for this and he wants the ball."

With Steven Kwan's second-half resurgence, rookie punch from Chase DeLauter and Travis Bazzana, and Jose Ramírez back from a hamate injury, this was supposed to be the year the Guardians were not an all-pitch, no-hit team.

The Guardians have scored three runs in three games, mustering seven hits against that cavalcade of White Sox arms. Perhaps the multiple looks will catch up to Chicago: Both Kay and Taylor looked more vulnerable their second time in front of the Guardians' bats.

Or maybe Cleveland is simply destined to run out of offensive juice.

They've made three playoff runs now under manager Stephen Vogt and have played 15 postseason games. They've been shut out three times and held to three or fewer runs in five other games.

Now, they'll need to turn it around and then sustain three solid offensive games.

"Two games. Unfortunately, it is two games that are in the postseason," says Vogt. "A little bit of try to do too much, a little bit of maybe not ready to hit your pitch at times.

"Again, we have had two games stretches like this all year and we come right back. I got a lot of faith in this offense. I have a lot of faith in this team. Like I said, this team plays its best with its back against the wall. I am looking forward to getting out on the field on Wednesday."

Vogt might not understand what his club is getting into. White Sox fans have existed in a state somewhere between disbelief and delirium. And now, postseason papal power will find its way to the South Side.

The White Sox narrowly lost the Central title to Cleveland, forcing them on the road for four consecutive playoff games.

Now that they've survived it and return home undefeated, what might Rate Field sound like in Wednesday's potential clinching Game 3?

"It's all we are talking about. We are about to go back to a zoo," pitcher Davis Martin told reporters in Cleveland. "It's going to be wild. It's going to be crazy.

"If Mune (Murakami) hits a ball 900 feet, it's going to be loud as heck. We are all excited to hear it and be a part of it."

articles.title: As Halo Moves to Activision, Halo Studios Writers Tease What Might Have Been
articles.summary: Following the launch of Halo: Campaign Evolved, Halo Studios has put out a blog post detailing plans for the future of Master Chief’s story. It’s an interesting look at where the series might have gone, prior to the recent announcement that Activision is now the shepherd of the Halo series.
articles.body:
Following the launch of Halo: Campaign Evolved , Halo Studios has put out a blog post detailing plans for the future of Master Chief’s story. It’s an interesting look at where the series might have gone, prior to the recent announcement that Activision is now the shepherd of the Halo series .

The next Halo game was reportedly still years away , but the blog post, penned by Halo franchise writer Alex Wakeford, gives us a peek behind the curtain with hints about the studio’s plans, but also an attempt at canonizing a story that’s been told through games, remakes, books, and TV. You can check out the blog post for its list of retcons and continuity clarifications.

While the majority of the blog was written prior to the Xbox reshuffle, when Halo Studios thought the series was still in its hands, there are addendums written prior to the news breaking. At one point, Wakeford joked that you’ll have to wait until next week to find out more about the Sacristan Order, before dropping a note: “This joke sure took on new dimensions after last week's news.”

Elsewhere, Wakeford talked about the next novel by Troy Denning, titled Halo: Fireteam Noble. “Many have been asking whether this novel will still be releasing,” Wakeford said. “To this we can say that it is absolutely our intent to see this project cross the finish line. Troy has written a fantastic story and a good chunk of the editorial process has been conducted.”

Another novel, Halo: Burn the Road Home, written by senior franchise writer at Halo Studios, Kenneth Peters, is also in the works, though its future is as uncertain as Fireteam Noble. There’s no word on whether preorders will get a refund if the projects don’t make it over the line.

We also have official art of the Primordial, by Sam Wood. The Primordial would go on to become the Gravemind from Halo 2. "A creature of horrifying providence and intent known by many names — the Timeless One, the Primordial, and eventually the Gravemind," Wakeford said. "This twisted progeny of the Precursors was executed by Bornstellar through the use of a timelock on Gyre 11, reducing its form to dust by subjecting it to the passage of millions of years in mere moments. But the Primordial's experiments had borne fruit. Having infected itself with the Flood, the consciousness of this strange being passed into the parasite's hive mind where it is awakened whenever the Flood successfully form a compound intelligence."

Perhaps the most interesting bit of information for Halo lore fans comes at the end of the blog post with a tease of the Xalanyn, children of Abaddon. "THE ENDLESS EMERGE," Wakeford declared. "And finally, as is tradition, we’ll leave you with something that hopefully sparks your imagination and lets your canon curiosities run wild with endless questions."

The Xalanyn are an advanced race of immortal beings whose members were imprisoned by the Forerunners. The suggestion here is Halo 7, or whatever Halo Studios' now scrapped next Halo game would have been called, would have revealed more of the mysterious overarching antagonists.

The concept art is very cool and makes me a bit sad that Halo will probably never see them. It’s about time Halo got some new enemies to chew through. Instead, Halo will probably become Xbox’s Call of Duty (let’s pretend Call of Duty isn’t Xbox’s Call of Duty, for the sake of argument).

Halo Studios’ final game in the series was released globally on July 28, 2026, with IGN’s Halo: Campaign Evolved review praising the “gunplay that revolutionized first-person console games” which makes it still “worth playing today.” The game was a testbed for a switch to the Unreal Engine, following a middling launch for Halo Infinite , which used the studio’s proprietary Slipspace Engine.

Yesterday, people at Ninja Theory announced layoffs following the Xbox reshuffle that resulted in the studio closing down. Staff at Gears of War: E-Day developer The Coalition are also reportedly expecting layoffs , despite positive reviews of the studio’s latest game.

articles.title: GTA 6 Won't Be 'Too Specific About Any Particular Person, Event, or Movement,' Rockstar Says GTA Has Never Focused on 'National Politics'
articles.summary: Rockstar apparently isn’t interested in making a political statement in GTA 6.
articles.body:
Rockstar apparently isn’t interested in making a political statement in GTA 6 , a game about love, passion, and the shrinking of the American dream. In the company’s defense, its reasoning is sound. Rockstar has never been scared to push the boat, with GTA 5 famously touching on the effectiveness of torture and government blacksites, and GTA 6 will likely be no different.

The line is drawn at political satire via real-world moments. If GTA 6 had created an NPC called Melon Husk who shoots rockets into space and is a bit weird, by the time it came out it wouldn’t have factored in all the horrible stuff that character’s real-life counterpart has done since. These games take a long time to make, and no one wants to be as dated as a Borderlands gag.

"If you go back to previous GTAs, there's never really been much focus on national politics," Rupert Humphries, senior vice president of narrative of Rockstar, told Love Magazine . "The rise of Homeland Security and the Patriot Act were pretty central to GTA 4, but that was mainly because post-9/11 New York was a real frontline for those issues.

In Pictures: How GTA 6's Jason and Lucia Have Evolved Since 2023

“Because we are trying to make games that feel very specific to the moment they are released, but at the same time, not reflective of the exact world we live in, we don't want to be too specific about any particular person, event, movement or anything like that.”

Instead, the focus is on capturing the essence of Florida — all the wild Florida men and women, cops and gangbangers the developer met on its GTA 6 research trips . “We have really tried to build out our world — filling it with all the characters and culture wars necessary to make it feel alive,” Humphries said.

“And then we have so many ways to tell these stories outside of actually meeting characters face to face. You can see a sign for an election, receive a robocall from a campaign, or hear a commercial on the radio. And then we have some great political talk shows on the radio too where they discuss all these issues.”

The focus is telling it all through the lens of satire, making it larger than life. Rockstar isn’t shying away from themes and contemporary topics, but rather than holding up a mirror and saying “remember this?” it’s attempting to explore those topics through its own original characters and scenarios.

GTA 6 features dual protagonists, Jason and Lucia, who embark upon a crime spree across a fictionalized rendition of Florida, called Leonida in-game. Local NBA team the Miami Heat will wear GTA 6-themed uniforms in its upcoming match to celebrate the game’s upcoming launch.

GTA 6 comes to PS5 and Xbox Series consoles on November 19, 2026. GTA 6 is expected to make up to $5.2 billion in sales by the end of launch week . The previous game continues to break records — GTA 5 has sold over 200 million copies across consoles and PC.

Technically, it's not an official GTA 6 console bundle; the game and hardware are purchased separately, but the promotion still effectively rewards anyone planning to upgrade their console ahead of what will likely be the biggest game release of all time.

The savings aren't instant, however. Best Buy says eligible customers will receive their $50 promotional certificate in their My Best Buy account around November 25, 2026, meaning you'll need to wait several months before cashing in the bonus credit.

PlayStation 5 - Digital Edition 1TB - Certified Refurbished

I'd also recommend considering a certified refurbished PS5 directly from PlayStation through the PS Direct store . A refurbished PS5 is currently $549, while the refurbished PS5 Digital Edition is $499.

That makes the choice between Best Buy and PlayStation a little more interesting. For the same price, PS Direct option gets you the newer PS5 design with 1TB of storage, although you'll be giving up Best Buy's $50 reward certificate deal.

If you're happy with digital games, the $499 refurbished PS5 Digital Edition is arguably the most compelling option of the lot, particularly if GTA 6 is the main reason you're buying a console in the first place .

I'd still recommend thinking carefully before going all-in on digital, though. The disc-drive PS5 gives you access to used games, physical discounts, borrowing and reselling games, so that extra $50 isn't necessarily money wasted. But if you have no existing physical library and are comfortable buying digitally, saving that money upfront is certainly a tempting proposition.

Honestly? Probably, yeah. While Amazon's October Prime Day sale ( Prime Big Deal Days ) is a good opportunity to grab a few good deals, more often than not these offers will reappear in a month or less, as they were, or as even better deals. If you can hold out, I'll always recommend waiting a little bit longer in order to save that bit more.

That being said, there is a rare chance that certain deals appear that are worth picking up ASAP. I, and the rest of my team, will often try to call these bargains out as and when we can, so you have the best opportunity to bag them. Otherwise, consider the rest of this article a helpful guide to what's on sale, what you can pick up if you so choose to, and the prices to look for when the Black Friday sales eventually roll around in November.

The only other reason I'd ever suggest not waiting is if you value your time over your money. Now it seems like an obvious statement, but it's not always a luxury we all get to have. If you do desperately want to play that game like right now and it's driving you insane, or your TV just broke, or you lost your headphones, sales like this are a great opportunity to pay yourself in time, so you don't have to stress or fret about something. Whatever the case, do what is best for you. I'm just a silly little guy, writing about silly little deals, on a silly little website.

articles.title: The Witcher Box Set Is At the Lowest Price We've Seen All Year
articles.body:
Amazon's Prime Big Deal Days sale has arrived, dropping the paperback Witcher box set is down to its lowest price all year. You can grab the five-book collection for $39.99, down from $89.99, saving you 47% off of the sticker price. This collection goes on sale often, but now's a good time to pick it up if you've been wanting to jump into the book saga alongside The Witcher 3 Remastered .

The box set includes only the five mainline Witcher books , so you won't get the two short story collections; The Last Wish and Sword of Destiny (which are also currently on sale for Prime Big Deal Days). But as those are supplemental additions, you can still enjoy the main stories without having read them, but we highly recommend doing so. This collection also doesn't include the most recen release, Crossroads of Ravens, the latest book in the series that serves as a prequel. You can still find it on sale at Amazon for $15 (25% off) in paperpack , though.

IGN recently had the opportunity to interview Witcher author and creator Andrzej Sapkowski , where we chatted about future adaptations, new books, and where the franchise is headed. Sapkowski's short story collections are good introductions to the world of the Witcher, and the author is considering penning even more short stories, saying "[i]t is not an easy thing to create a good short story. This is much more difficult than writing a novel . . . yes, I am considering writing more short stories".

Listen to the Full-Cast Audiobooks With the Audible Sale

The Witcher books have been getting the full-cast audiobook treatment this year. Only the prequel, Crossroads of Ravens, has been released so far, but two more audiobooks are set to follow in November 2026. If you'd prefer to try these out rather than reading the paperbacks, there's currently an Audible deal that makes it worth your while.

For a limited time, you can get the first three months of Audible Standard for $0.99 per month as well as a free $20 credit. The offer is available for new and returning subscribers, and essentially get you the first three full-cast Witcher audiobooks for only a few dollars.

articles.title: Ubisoft Will Reportedly Try Relaunching Watch Dogs: Legion With a Director's Cut
articles.summary: Ubisoft will attempt to relaunch Watch Dogs: Legion next year via a revamped Director's Cut, it's been reported.
articles.body:
Ubisoft will attempt to relaunch Watch Dogs: Legion next year via a revamped Director's Cut, it's been reported.

Legion launched back in 2020 to a somewhat tepid reaction, and the once-promising franchise has subsequently been rested, with no all-new game believed to be in development. But there is a push to do more with Legion early next year, Insider Gaming has reported — something that IGN has also heard through its own sources.

Watch Dogs: Legion divided fans by ditching the series' single-protagonist focus, and instead allowing you to play as any NPC from its virtual recreation of post-Brexit London. In practice, though, that meant playing as one of various archetypes (builder, hooligan, spy) who could be killed off if you failed missions.

Later DLC added Watch Dogs 1's Aiden Pearce and Watch Dogs 2's Wrench as playable characters, before an Assassin's Creed expansion attempted to reignite interest with a fun but non-canonical crossover featuring a descendant of Assassin's Creed Syndicate's Jacob and Evie Fry.

What could Watch Dogs: Legion Director's Cut contain? It seems likely to expect the above content to be included from the off, and perhaps more of a focus on the series' more recognizable faces, rather than that ability to play as anyone — but time will tell.

Watch Dogs: Legion creative director Clint Hocking abruptly parted ways with Ubisoft earlier this year, despite being in the middle of leading development on Assassin's Creed Hexe. Subsequently, Hocking said the experience of leading a large team within Ubisoft had been like working while "flaming barrels [are] falling down from a construction site," akin to a scene from the arcade game Donkey Kong .

This month, Ubisoft boss Yves Guillemot acknowledged the fact that Watch Dogs hadn't been named alongside its other major franchises as a focus for the company following its recent restructure, but said it was still considered "an important brand for the future." In the meantime, it remains unclear what is happening with the long-planned Watch Dogs movie project that wrapped production two years ago and had reshoots last year, but still lacks a release date.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

articles.title: GTA 5 Made Playable in Browser as AI-Generated Game Chaos Continues
articles.summary: Grand Theft Auto 5 was made playable in a browser before it was pulled offline, amid an explosion of AI-fueled games across the internet.
articles.body:
Grand Theft Auto 5 was made playable in a browser before it was pulled offline, amid an explosion of AI-fueled games across the internet.

Footage of GTA 5 running in a browser spread via social media yesterday, though the game's website is now offline — with reports that hosting service Cloudflare stepped in to intervene.

This latest development follows last week's cease and desist sent by Bethesda to block the AI-generated Fallout: New York fan project , which was also made playable via a PC browser. That game had been built by Claude Opus 5.5, and it seems likely that the PC build of GTA 5 was compiled similarly.

GTA 5 is now playable on web browser Here I am playing GTA 5 on chrome — Pixel Gamer 4k (@4k_isn) October 6, 2026

GTA 5 is now playable on web browser Here I am playing GTA 5 on chrome

The owner of the GTA 5 browser website is now asking "Who wants the source code?" — Pixel Gamer 4k (@4k_isn) October 6, 2026

The owner of the GTA 5 browser website is now asking "Who wants the source code?"

Last week, IGN reported on the original Xbox version of Halo: Combat Evolved, which was made available to play in a web browser . This is not a port of Bungie’s seminal 2001 first-person shooter, rather the original Xbox game running in your browser.

There's no doubting the popularity of these AI-built clones or derivative games, with images and gameplay videos being shared widely on social media alongside impressed responses from fans. But the owners of these franchises such as Rockstar and Bethesda will inevitably take a dim view of what they will likely see as piracy — particularly in the case of GTA 5's port.

Still, it remains to be seen exactly how the rapid progress of AI will be checked — or how AI-generated versions of popular games will be policed in future, beyond publishers simply playing whack-a-mole as popular examples pop up.

In Pictures: How GTA 6's Jason and Lucia Have Evolved Since 2023

AI is making what was traditionally a painstaking process of reverse-engineering and recompilation significantly faster, which has prompted some to wonder about the future of commercial video game development. Why buy a Switch 2 if you can have AI generate a clone of one of Nintendo's exclusives for free in your browser?

Others, though, have pointed out that none of the "game-merging" mods or clones display any creativity or present any new ideas, rather take existing popular video games and either mash them together or simply replicate what is already playable better elsewhere.

The question for Rockstar and parent company Take-Two now is, how long will it take for GTA 6 to be made playable in a browser, and what can it do to stop it?

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

articles.title: Carrie Forever: Every Adaptation of the Stephen King Story and Why You Should Watch Them All (More or Less)
articles.summary: Carrie Forever: We catalogue every version of Stephen King's Carrie ever just in time for the new Mike Flanagan adaptation.
articles.body:
The first Stephen King book ever published — the 1974 bestseller, Carrie — immediately put the horror writer on the map, and also led to it quickly becoming the first King story to be adapted for another medium with Brian De Palma’s 1976 film version. King would turn out to be a shockingly prolific writer who went on to write a staggering amount of work filled with tons of beloved, instantly recognizable characters in the decades since. Yet still — even with the likes of IT, The Shining, Pet Sematary, and so many more that have now been given multiple incarnations — Carrie stands out for how many times it’s been adapted. In fact, almost no other King project really comes close… except for the strange case of Children of the Corn and its 11 (!) movies, most of which were straight-to-video projects few ever mention.

It’s easy to see why Carrie continues to be revisited. King’s horror-tragedy about a sheltered teenage girl raised by a domineering religious mother and bullied by her classmates, only to lash out in bloody revenge thanks to her hidden telekinetic powers, feels like a dark fairy tale of sorts. Its touchstones, most especially the prom that ends the story — and the image of Carrie covered in pig’s blood thanks to a diabolical prank, beginning her murderous rampage — are iconic and unforgettable.

October sees the debut of yet another version of Carrie, this time told in an expanded form as a streaming series from acclaimed filmmaker, television creator, and frequent King adapter Mike Flanagan. So with Carrie 2026 here, let’s look back at all of the adaptations we’ve gotten so far, from the beloved to the best left forgotten.

The gold standard of Carrie adaptations, Brian De Palma’s film is still the one that all others are compared to 50 years later, and still counted amongst the best King adaptations for all of his work. Yes, there are some very dated and silly 1970s fashions and stylistic flourishes in the film, and a couple of puzzling diversions, such as a tux-renting comic relief montage featuring Carrie’s prom date, Tommy (William Katt), alongside two guys who barely register as characters outside of this one sequence. But De Palma’s film still expertly captures the essence of King’s book and its inherent tragedy, aided in no small part by his terrific casting choices of the excellent Sissy Spacek as Carrie and Piper Laurie as her mother, Margaret.

Both women received well-deserved Oscar nominations for their roles, and the film benefits from great casting across the board, including Amy Irving as Carrie’s sympathetic classmate, the regretful Sue Snell, and Nancy Allen as the nasty Chris Hargensen, who will ultimately push Carrie over the edge.

And of course, De Palma absolutely nails the prom sequence. Spacek bathed in blood is an all-time classic cinematic image, and his audacious use of split-screen effects to track the mayhem that follows as Carrie begins to kill her classmates works incredibly well.

The 1980s stand out as the only decade since Carrie’s publication in the ’70s without a new movie or TV project based on the book, but that didn’t mean nothing was happening on the Carrie front. An infamous stage musical arrived to get plenty of attention in all the wrong ways.

Though it shared the same writer as the 1976 film, Lawrence D. Cohen, and even one cast member — Betty Buckley, who played gym teacher Miss Collins (renamed from the book’s Miss Desjardin) in the film, and was cast as Margaret for this production – Carrie: The Musical hardly got the same response. Burdened by a notably high budget while still navigating major technical difficulties thanks to its tricky effects, and with original songs that received, at best, divisive responses, the show was greeted by some audible boos according to reports at the time.

Carrie would close after only 16 previews and 5 official performances, cementing its legacy as a legendary bomb… or as the New York Times called it, “the most expensive quick flop in Broadway history.” But perhaps it’s only fitting for a story that has been resurrected so many times that this wouldn’t be the end for Carrie: The Musical. But we’ll get back to that…

The only Carrie story to date to serve as any sort of continuation or sequel came in this late ’90s follow-up to the 1976 film, which centered on Rachel (Emily Bergl), a teenage girl who doesn’t initially know she is actually Carrie White’s half-sister. And yes, she has the same powers. (King’s book establishes that there are other telekinetics, all women, but that men are the carriers of the “TK” gene. Carrie’s father, Ralph, is dead prior to the events of the book, but De Palma’s movie never mentions him, allowing for this sequel to suggest that he’s somewhere out there, getting other women pregnant with more telekinetic girls).

The Rage is one of those sequels that effectively functions as a remake. Rachel just so happens to also be an outcast girl who also has an awful home life — this time thanks to crappy foster parents — and who will also eventually be made to think she’s been accepted by her cool classmates only for a cruel prank to occur, this time at a house party and not the prom, with a sex tape of her and the boy she liked being played for all to see taking the place of the pig’s blood. The end result is the same; everyone laughs, and then everyone dies.

The Rage was a turbulent production, initially developed as a completely independent story before being reshaped into a Carrie sequel. The original director was replaced mid-production over the dreaded “creative differences,” with Katt Shea (Poison Ivy) replacing him. There’s an interesting use of a real-life story — and a reflection of the odious ways young men can treat young women — in its depiction of a group of guys who cruelly seduce and then discard every girl they can just to rank them with their friends. And there’s some fun to be had with Rachel’s pseudo-gothy look and the baffling but visually cool way that vine-like tattoos cover her body and face during her massacre. Sadly, though, The Rage is a pretty “whatever” movie overall. It’s also frustrating as hell on the legacy sequel front, with its one big returning character — Amy Irving back as Sue Snell — dispatched in an incredibly unceremonious way.

However, The Rage: Carrie 2 is at least a pretty amusing time capsule of a teen movie that came out in 1999, featuring plenty of touchstones of the era, including a ska song, a character quoting Scream, and the presence of Mena Suvari.

Carrie made her first foray into television for this 2002 NBC TV movie, which is notable at this point because it was written by none other than Bryan Fuller a decade before he would create one of the best horror TV projects of all time (for NBC no less) with Hannibal. Fuller was the first person to utilize some of the true crime-style angle that the book is filled with, as King’s original story includes all sorts of excerpts from testimony, books, and other responses that occurred after Carrie’s massacre. The pared-down version here finds Sue Snell (Battlestar Galactica’s Kandyse McClure) and others speaking to the police about what happened as part of a framing device.

Fuller also brought back some other elements excised from the book in the 1976 film, including meeting the father (Michael Kopsa) of Chris (Lost’s Emilie de Ravin), a powerful lawyer trying to bully away the trouble his daughter got into by being a bully. Overall though, director ​​David Carson (Star Trek: Generations) delivers a functional version of the story that’s lacking in energy and longer than it needs to be.

Angela Bettis is quite good as Carrie and makes her distinct from Spacek’s version, though it’s notable how little Margaret resonates here. Despite being played by another great actress, Patricia Clarkson, she feels strangely peripheral thanks to a combination of being offscreen for long periods, and because Clarkson — perhaps in an effort by either herself, Carson, or both to not mimic Piper Laurie’s bombastic performance — plays the role as oddly subdued.

There is one other aspect of Carrie 2002 that stands out, and that’s the ending… Because Carrie White lives! Unlike King’s book or the other adaptations, she doesn’t die the night of the prom, but is instead saved by Sue, who sneaks her out of town. This ending was included because the Carrie TV-movie was actually intended as a backdoor pilot for a potential TV series, though that obviously didn't come to be.

Perhaps not shockingly given its somewhat camp appeal, a bit of a cult following grew around the infamous flop that was the 1988 Carrie Broadway musical, leading to some unofficial productions being staged in the years afterward, including one at Emerson College (hello to my alma mater). But in 2012, the risky decision was made to officially bring Carrie back, this time as an Off-Broadway revival. Both Lawrence D. Cohen — whose ongoing connection to Carrie is pretty notable at this point — and the original composers, Michael Gore and Dean Pitchford, returned for what was a rather massive reworking of the show, attempting to make it more focused on the psychological drama aspects. Much of it was rewritten, with seven of the songs from the original production dropped and new songs replacing them.

And lo and behold, this time it went over well! The new version received far better reviews than the original, and going forward, this was now the version that would be used for future productions. The revamped Carrie musical would go on to 2015 runs in both London’s West End and in Los Angeles, which were also well received.

The LA production was an immersive theater production that slightly tweaked the 2012 revamp’s dialogue and songs, including restoring a few verses from songs that were there in 1988 but removed in 2012. The staging was much more grandiose, with gallons of blood dropped from the rafters, select floor seats that would be moved during the show with the action, and other immersive elements like some audience members getting to join in and dance at the prom (before all the death stuff, naturally). Its success would lead to a second limited engagement of the show later that same year.

A 2018 episode of Riverdale involved characters on that show performing in a production of Carrie, and included several songs from the production, meaning that showrunner Roberto Aguirre-Sacasa was once more involved with telling Carrie’s story, in a manner of speaking, after writing the 2013 film.

Carrie returned to movie screens for yet another remake in 2013, this time with an impressive pedigree that included director Kimberly Peirce — whose 1999 film Boys Don’t Cry had received two Oscar nominations and ultimately secured Hilary Swank her first Academy Award — and a buzzed-about star in Chloë Grace Moretz.

There was some discussion at the time of Moretz simply being too attractive to play the unpopular Carrie, which felt overblown. Yes, King describes her in the book as a bit overweight and pimply — something that no adaptation has ever tried to replicate — but when she gets dressed up for the prom, he also makes it explicit that she looks genuinely beautiful, and it’s made clear the things that make Carrie an outcast stem from her upbringing and demeanor, and not her looks. But the big issue with Carrie 2013 was simply its feeling of sameness, and that it was too beholden to De Palma’s beloved movie instead of finding its own unique take.

Yes, it’s the first version to include smart phones as part of a modern day bully’s arsenal, but it’s by and large echoing the 1976 film, including using enough of its structure and even dialogue from that film to the point that Lawrence D. Cohen received a screenwriting credit alongside the film’s actual writer, Roberto Aguirre-Sacasa, despite not writing anything new this time.

Once more, performances aren’t an issue, with Moretz and yet another excellent actress as Margaret, Julianne Moore, having some strong moments playing off one another. Judy Greer is also an inspired choice to play Miss Desjardin, who feels a bit more prominent than in previous versions. Nevertheless, Carrie 2013 feels like a missed opportunity to really shake up the story by sticking too close to what came before.

And that brings us to the newest version, as Carrie returns via a modern-day streaming series for Prime Video. Tackling Carrie yet again is obviously a tricky endeavor that on the surface makes fans wary given how much it’s been done; just look at all of those examples above! But there’s a reason to be optimistic, because this time the man guiding the series is Mike Flanagan, who not only has made several acclaimed series at this point — including The Haunting of Hill House and Midnight Mass — but is also a massive Stephen King fan who’s already given us strong adaptations of King’s work that include Gerald’s Game and Doctor Sleep .

With the blessing of King himself, who’s serving as an Executive Producer, Flanagan has greatly reworked the story, starting with having Carrie (Summer H. Howell) now just beginning school for the first time ever, having been hidden away at home by Margaret (Samantha Sloyan). With the story now taking place over an entire semester, Flanagan told IGN he felt like he had the opportunity to better focus on what modern-day high school kids deal with, including violence in school and “what cruelty and bullying can be in a world where every single one of those incidents and any mistakes you make in your formative years can be broadcast permanently for the world to see on the internet.” Flanagan is also including glimpses of other young women with telekinesis in the series, noting that in the book, “King is explicit that [Carrie’s] not alone in this,” even if Carrie herself is unaware of that fact.

You can see the end result for yourself when Carrie debuts October 7.
